title: Kid-Safe 'Freckle' Phone Builds Independence
paragraphs: Having a smartphone can keep kids in contact with family while they build independence. But parents might worry about the access these phones offer to things like social media and other addictive apps.

This is why US company Freckle has made a smartphone for children aged 7 to 13. It uses its own operating system, ClayOS, that doesn't give kids access to an unlimited web browser, an app store or social media.

Instead, the Freckle phone offers its own built-in apps and features that parents can control access to with a companion app they download onto their own phone. This lets parents decide what their children can use.
For example, the Freckle phone can be used to call and text — but only with contacts added by parents. Two Freckle phones can also be paired so kids can use them as walkie-talkies.
There's a tap-to-pay feature, but parents add the money and set spending limits.

Freckle is made for fun and exploration too. Its Quests feature lets parents send their kids out on an educational mission. This might be finding five different insects in the park, or using Freckle's camera to take a photo of something that's older than them in a museum.

The Discovery Camera app also lets kids find out about things they take photos of. If they take a picture of a bird or an interesting plant, Freckle can tell them more about it using age-appropriate language.
Its Why Chat can also answer kids' questions in the same way — but the company said if the question would be better asked of a real adult, Freckle tells users to go to a parent instead.
For now, Freckle is only on sale in the US. It's available for pre-order at a cost of $199, with shipping planned for December 2026.
